affectedLayers: infrastructure (IUnitOfWork, INotificationService, IEmployeeService, IAuditService — consumed unchanged)

successCriteria.description: A SUBMITTED cancellation produces EXACTLY TWO notificationService.create calls: one to the requester (existing, unchanged) and one to the requester's direct manager, resolved as (await employeeService.getEmployeeById(request.employeeId)).managerId.

An APPROVED cancellation (the GP-008 reversal path) produces EXACTLY TWO notificationService.create calls: one to the requester and one to the ORIGINAL row's request.approverId — never the reversal row's approverId (which is null by construction).
A DRAFT cancellation produces EXACTLY ONE notificationService.create call (the requester only) — no approver notification, matching the rule that a DRAFT cancellation touches no balance.

The approver notification carries relatedEntityType 'leave_request', relatedEntityId = the ORIGINAL request id, relatedEntityCode = request.leaveTypeCode (carried verbatim), and type = the existing literal 'leave_request' — no new discriminator, no new shared type, no new DTO.

A null resolved recipient never fails the cancellation: a SUBMITTED request whose requester has managerId === null, and an APPROVED request whose approverId is null, both complete successfully (no throw, no ConflictError), emit exactly ONE notification (requester only), and record the skip in the CANCEL audit entry's afterState payload.

The approver notification is emitted even when the cancelling actor IS the resolved recipient (a manager cancelling a direct report's SUBMITTED request; the recorded approver cancelling their own approval) — no self-authored marker, no suppression, so the two-notification count stays unconditional.

The approver notification is created inside the SAME existing uow.withTransaction callback as the requester notification, with the same client threaded through: uow.callCount === 1 and the stub PoolClient is forwarded to the approver notification's create call.

The CANCEL audit entry is unchanged in shape: exactly one entry per cancellation, action AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, entityId = the ORIGINAL request id on both the in-place and reversal paths, with beforeState/afterState still populated (only afterState may carry the skip marker).

The requester notification is byte-identical in shape to before this phase (same recipientId = request.employeeId, same type/title/message/relatedEntityType/relatedEntityId), and the DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place path, the APPROVED reversal path's balance release, the double-cancel guard, assertCanCancel, and the timing guard are all unmodified.

resolveApproverRecipient is invoked once per cancellation and BEFORE the transaction opens (it reads the employee, not the transaction), so no employee read occurs inside the withTransaction callback.

constraints: Scope is ONE file: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts. No other src/ file may change — in particular leave.model.ts, leave.repository.ts, notification.model.ts, notification.service.ts, notification.service.interface.ts, leave.routes.ts, and src/shared/types are fixed contracts from Phases 1-2.

The notification set is a function of the STATE CHANGE, not of who performed it: exactly TWO notificationService.create calls for SUBMITTED and APPROVED cancellations, exactly ONE for DRAFT. Do NOT add a recipient list/array column to the notifications table and do NOT introduce a fan-out abstraction.

A missing recipient NEVER fails the cancellation: no ConflictError, no assert-and-fail, no transitive escalation, no ADMIN broadcast, no backfill. The skip is recorded in the CANCEL audit entry's afterState payload only; the audit entry's shape (action, entityType, entityId, beforeState/afterState presence) stays unchanged.

The approver notification's relatedEntityId is ALWAYS the ORIGINAL request id — on the GP-008 reversal path the reversal row's id must never be used (the reversal row carries approverId = null by construction, so reading the recipient or the id from it would silently drop every notification on that path).

No new shared type, DTO, enum member, module, or notification discriminator: type stays the existing literal 'leave_request', title/message are composed inline in leave, and relatedEntityCode reuses the Phase 2 nullable column rather than a leave-specific field.

Transaction boundary: the service owns the unit of work. The approver notification joins the EXISTING uow.withTransaction callback with the same client threaded through; no second/nested withTransaction, no repository opening BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, and no pool or module-level db helper imported into the service.

resolveApproverRecipient is a private helper on LeaveService taking the LeaveRequest and returning Promise<string | null>; it is called once per cancellation BEFORE the transaction opens, because it reads the employee (not the transaction). It must not be added to ILeaveService.

Do NOT modify LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, the DRAFT/SUBMITTED in-place path, the APPROVED reversal path's balance release, the double-cancel guard (findByReversesRequestId), assertCanCancel, or the timing guard (startDate <= today -> ConflictError).
Strict TypeScript (no implicit any, strict null checks) and the no-any rule: the nullable recipient is narrowed with an explicit null check, not a non-null assertion or a cast.
No route change, no listPendingDecisions, and no tests in this phase (Phases 4-6). The existing requester notification call site is left untouched.
outOfScope: Any change to src/modules/leave/leave.routes.ts, including a new endpoint or a role guard — the route surface is Phase 5.
Any test file under tests/ (including extending tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts) — Phase 6.
Any change to src/modules/notification/ (model, repository, service, interface) or to the notifications table DDL — the relatedEntityCode contract is fixed from Phases 1-2.
Any change to src/modules/leave/leave.model.ts, leave.repository.ts, or src/shared/types — LeaveRequest, CreateLeaveRequestInput, PendingDecision, and the shared enums are fixed contracts.
Escalation, ADMIN broadcast, recipient backfill, or any repair of the legacy null-approverId state — the gap is recorded in the audit entry and left visible, not fixed.
Any change to the web application root (web/src/) — the approvals queue consumer is Phase 7 (optional).
Notification delivery/status advancement (PENDING -> SENT/READ) or a BullMQ fan-out job — the cancellation notification is created PENDING and is not advanced by this phase.

ambiguities.description: The exact shape of the "skip marker" recorded in the CANCEL audit entry's afterState when the resolved recipient is null. The intent fixes only that the marker lives in afterState and that the entry's shape (action/entityType/entityId/beforeState/afterState) is unchanged — it does not name a key or a wrapper. Phase 6 must assert the skip is recorded, so the shape needs to be stable enough to assert.
options: A named key merged into the existing afterState object (e.g. a boolean/string field alongside the updated or reversal row's fields)
A nested metadata object under a single named key on afterState, leaving the row's own fields untouched
A string appended to an existing free-text field of afterState

ambiguities.description: Whether resolveApproverRecipient is invoked (and thus performs an employee read) for a DRAFT cancellation, where its result is unused. The intent says it is called "once per cancellation, BEFORE the transaction", while rule 1 says DRAFT notifies nobody else — so a DRAFT call is permitted but its null result is by design, not a skip.
options: Call it for every cancellation including DRAFT, and ignore the result for DRAFT (no skip marker, since DRAFT has no recipient by design)
Short-circuit before calling it for DRAFT, so no employee read occurs on the DRAFT path

ambiguities.description: Whether the skip marker is also recorded when the resolved recipient is non-null but the notification is not emitted for some other reason — the intent only defines the null-recipient skip. No other suppression path is specified, so the marker should be tied strictly to the null-recipient case.
options: Marker is emitted ONLY when the resolved recipient is null (the single defined skip case)
Marker is emitted whenever the approver notification is not created, for any reason

ambiguities.description: Whether the approver notification's title/message must differ from the requester's. The intent gives an example title ('Leave request cancelled') identical to the existing requester notification's title and says the message may mention the leave type, but does not require distinct copy. Phase 6 asserts on recipient, relatedEntityId, relatedEntityCode and type — not on copy.
options: Copy may be identical to the requester notification's; only recipient and the related-entity fields are contractual
Copy must be distinct (e.g. naming the requester or the leave type) so the two notifications are humanly distinguishable

ambiguities.description: Documented-vs-built drift adjacent to this phase: .gestalt/architecture/reconciled.json's Phase 2 rationale states the pending-decisions query MUST also exclude reverses_request_id IS NOT NULL (a cancelled-after-approval request is two rows, so the reversal row would be a spurious queue entry), but the implemented PgLeaveRequestRepository.findPendingDecisions filters on status = 'SUBMITTED' only. This phase does not change the queue, but its notification keying to the ORIGINAL request id assumes the reversal row is not a queue member.
options: Leave the queue predicate as built (status = 'SUBMITTED' only) and correct the reconciled architecture to match the implementation
Add the reverses_request_id IS NULL predicate to the repository in a later phase and keep the reconciled architecture as written

entityInvariants.invariant: Shape is unchanged (15 fields, no additions/renames). approverId is null while DRAFT/SUBMITTED and non-null only after a decision; it becomes load-bearing as the APPROVED-cancellation notification recipient. A null approverId on an APPROVED row is a reachable legacy state that must be tolerated, not repaired.

entityInvariants.entity: LeaveRequestReversal (the GP-008 reversal ROLE of LeaveRequest — non-null reversesRequestId, not a separate type)
entityInvariants.invariant: Born CANCELLED, terminal and inert, with approverId/approvalComment/submittedAt/decidedAt all null and reversesRequestId = the ORIGINAL request id. It is the row cancel RETURNS, but it is never the source of the notification recipient or of the notification's relatedEntityId.

Reused unchanged; created PENDING and not advanced by this phase. relatedEntityCode is nullable and generic (a code for whatever relatedEntityType names) — for a cancellation notification it carries the request's leaveTypeCode verbatim. type stays the existing literal 'leave_request'; no new discriminator and no leave-specific field.

Immutable and unchanged by this phase: exactly one CANCEL entry per cancellation, entityId = the ORIGINAL request id on both the in-place and reversal paths, beforeState = the original request, afterState = the updated/reversal row (plus the skip marker when the recipient was null). The approver notification must not be folded into, replace, or duplicate it.

Unchanged. managerId is the sole source of the SUBMITTED-cancellation recipient; a null managerId is a real domain case (no direct manager), not a data gap, and must not be treated as an error. A TERMINATED recorded approver is still a valid recipient.

Unchanged. The cancellation's balance release is untouched by this phase: DRAFT touches no balance row, SUBMITTED decrements pendingDays, APPROVED decrements usedDays — each read with forUpdate = true before the write, inside the same unit of work as the notifications.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Unchanged: assertAuthenticated first, then assertCanCancel (owner may cancel own DRAFT/SUBMITTED; otherwise only APPROVED, by the direct manager or an ADMIN). The approver notification adds no new authorization rule and no new role branch.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unchanged error set: UnauthorizedError (missing/invalid actor), ForbiddenError (assertCanCancel), NotFoundError (unknown id), ConflictError (timing guard, double-cancel guard). A null resolved recipient is NOT an error — the cancellation still resolves with the returned request.

interfaceConstraints.operation: LeaveService.resolveApproverRecipient(request: LeaveRequest): Promise<string | null> (private helper, not on ILeaveService)
interfaceConstraints.authRule: None — it performs no authorization; it only reads the employee record.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null rather than throwing when no recipient exists (DRAFT; SUBMITTED with managerId === null; APPROVED with approverId === null). It must not throw ConflictError or any other error for a missing recipient.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: Unchanged — no authorization in the notification service; the leave service owns who may cancel.
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Unchanged: ValidationError on a blank recipientId/type/title/message. The approver call must pass a non-blank recipientId (the resolved recipient) and a non-blank title/message, so a null recipient must be skipped rather than passed through. A throw here propagates and rolls back the whole cancellation unit of work.
Unchanged. Exactly one CANCEL entry per cancellation; the skip marker rides in afterState and must not change action, entityType, or entityId.

Unchanged — throws NotFoundError for an unknown id. It takes NO PoolClient, which is why recipient resolution happens before the transaction opens; it must not be called from inside the withTransaction callback.

Unchanged: any throw inside the callback rolls back the whole unit of work. The approver notification insert participates, so a failed insert rolls back the status change, the balance release, and the audit entry together.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Reuse the existing CreateNotificationInput shape and the Notification.relatedEntityCode field verbatim — do not re-declare, rename, or widen them, and do not add a leave-specific field. relatedEntityCode is optional at the call site and the repository persists null when omitted.

Match the existing notification call sites in this same file exactly in shape: recipientId, type: 'leave_request', title, message, relatedEntityType: 'leave_request', relatedEntityId, plus relatedEntityCode for the approver call — and pass the transaction client as the trailing argument.

Reuse the existing CANCEL audit entry construction unchanged: action AuditAction.CANCEL, entityType LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, entityId = the ORIGINAL request id, beforeState = the original request, afterState = the updated/reversal row. Only afterState may gain the skip marker.
consistencyRequirements.referencePath: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (the two existing auditService.record CANCEL calls) and src/shared/types (LEAVE_REQUEST_ENTITY_TYPE, AuditAction.CANCEL)

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Resolve the SUBMITTED recipient through the same injected employee service and the same call the existing authorization helpers already use — do not query the employee table directly and do not add a repository method.

Thread the transaction client as the optional trailing PoolClient argument on every participating call inside the callback, exactly as the existing cancel body does — no second transaction, no repository opening BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, no pool import in the service.
consistencyRequirements.referencePath: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (the existing uow.withTransaction callback in cancel) and AGENTS.md 'Architecture rules' item 5

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Keep the GP-008 reversal semantics intact: the original APPROVED row stays byte-identical, the reversal row is created with approverId null, and the notification's relatedEntityId is keyed to the ORIGINAL request id — never the reversal row's id.
consistencyRequirements.referencePath: src/modules/leave/leave.service.ts (the APPROVED branch of cancel) and docs/GOLDEN_PRINCIPLES.md GP-008

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The approver notification's relatedEntityCode carries request.leaveTypeCode verbatim as the canonical lowercase LeaveTypeCode enum value — no upper-casing, no mapping, no re-derivation.

Every state-changing operation still writes an audit record and all database access still goes through the injected repository/service interfaces — the new notification is an additional side effect inside the existing audited unit of work, not a replacement for the audit entry.

The existing 'Feature: Leave cancellation flow' section's notification contract (notifications table without related_entity_code; cancellation notifies only the affected employee) is superseded for this feature by the reconciled architecture's 'Feature: Notify the approver when a leave request is cancelled' section — the new section must be recorded rather than the old one silently contradicted.

integrationPoints.why: The approver notification is emitted through this existing contract with the transaction client threaded through; the interface is unchanged.
Sole source of the SUBMITTED-cancellation recipient via the requester's managerId; takes no client, so it is called before the transaction.
The CANCEL entry carries the skip marker in afterState while its shape stays unchanged.
The approver notification joins the existing cancellation unit of work; the service owns the boundary and the data-access layer opens it.
The ORIGINAL row read (findById) is the source of approverId and leaveTypeCode for the notification; the reversal row returned by create is never the notification's key. All unchanged.

integrationPoints.target: tests/unit/modules/leave/leave.service.test.ts — the existing eight in-memory fakes and recorded-call arrays
integrationPoints.why: Phase 6 asserts the two-notification count, the recipient, relatedEntityCode, the skip marker, and client forwarding through these existing seams; the phase must not require new fakes or a changed fake surface.
